analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/serving-stalls.md) and updates to docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (flowchart at lines 298-299 and a new paragraph at lines 338-372). No executable source is supplied, so I reviewed the described behavior against the threat model without verifying the underlying Swift implementation.

Described behavior: paged KV pools retain up to 1/8 of the slot grant (max 2 GiB) of free 64 MiB segments across requests. They reinstall them for the next admission. New segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages. Retained segments are uncommitted, dropped on refused charge or memory pressure, and returned after 30 s idle. The proactive buffer-cache sweep is now idle-gated, and load gates release retained segments before eviction.

Security-relevant questions for any pass that sees the code (A-001, T-028, T-041, TB-007):
1. Cross-request residue. Reinstalling a retained free segment for the next admission could expose a prior request's KV data to a different consumer if segments are not zeroed or overwritten before reuse. The docs say retention avoids 'allocating, zero-filling and fencing' new segments, which implies reuse without zero-fill. The pool's read-before-write discipline (page tables, lengths) is not visible here. T-028 already covers residual GPU memory, but this change adds a reuse path in-process.
2. Memory accounting. Retained segments are uncommitted, with no grant, floor or ledger charge. The docs state they are released before load gates evict or refuse, and that they are not counted as eviction credit once parked. This matters for availability (OOM under the process memory ledger) but is bounded by the 2 GiB cap and pressure-drop logic.
3. Rollback env flags (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION, _HOST_ZEROS, _IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP) are local operator controls and are not a trust escalation. The operator is already the adversary for process memory (T-014).

No concrete regression is evidenced by the documentation alone. The residue-on-reuse question is an unverified code contract, so I request deeper review of the segment reinstall path in code (CBv2RetainedKVSegments, PagedKVPool) instead of reporting a finding.
